text: Add a train-fitted user-by-hour interaction to let the additive scorer express user-specific time-of-day preferences.
rationale: Request context was the only positively screened feature family, while hour 16 has weak nDCG@5 despite moderate GAUC, indicating residual time-specific top-rank error. The prior user-by-tab cross produced only a small global gain, so this is a bounded test of a different context interaction rather than broad feature expansion.
exact_ablation: Relative to experiment 3, append exactly one train-fitted categorical user_id × hour interaction feature with an additive weight; retain user_id, video_id, tab, hour, weekday, user_id × tab, BCE loss, optimizer, split, and early stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by 0.000 to 0.002 if personal time-of-day preference improves within-user positive-negative ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.001 to 0.003 if hour-specific residuals promote long-view candidates into the top five, with the largest possible benefit in weak hour slices such as hour 16.

text: Add a train-fitted tab-by-hour interaction to capture request-context combinations not represented by separate additive context effects.
rationale: The positive request-context screen supports context as a family, and tab 0 and tab 6 have particularly poor top-five performance. A tab-by-hour term can model context combinations while avoiding unavailable behavioral or aggregate fields.
exact_ablation: Relative to experiment 3, append exactly one train-fitted categorical tab × hour interaction feature with an additive weight; retain every existing feature, model parameterization, BCE loss, optimizer, split, and early stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Change between -0.001 and +0.002 because the interaction may refine context-dependent ordering but can be sparse in uncommon combinations.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.001 to 0.003 if context-combination effects specifically correct top-five errors in high-volume weak tabs.

text: Add a train-fitted video-by-tab interaction so that a video's long-view propensity can vary by request surface.
rationale: The scorer's global metrics are driven almost entirely by warm items, while tab slices show major quality heterogeneity. A video-by-tab residual tests whether the same warm item is ranked differently across surfaces without using video metadata or outcome-derived aggregates.
exact_ablation: Relative to experiment 3, append exactly one train-fitted categorical video_id × tab interaction feature with an additive weight; leave all existing features, BCE loss, optimizer settings, split, and early stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by 0.000 to 0.002 if surface-specific video effects resolve within-user order among items shown in different tabs.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.000 to 0.003 if the residual corrects surface-specific head ranking; it may be flat if most within-user candidates share a tab.

text: Add a train-fitted user-by-weekday interaction to test stable weekly user-context preference beyond main effects.
rationale: Weekday is an eligible, complete-coverage request-context field that contributed to the sole positive feature-family screen. This interaction is lower-cardinality than user-by-hour and therefore offers a lower-variance personalization test.
exact_ablation: Relative to experiment 3, append exactly one train-fitted categorical user_id × weekday interaction feature with an additive weight; retain all current features, BCE loss, optimizer, split, and early stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by 0.000 to 0.0015 if recurring weekly preferences improve per-user ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.000 to 0.002 if weekly preference affects which candidates enter a user's top five; a flat result is plausible because the validation window covers only one week.

text: Replace row-mean BCE with inverse-training-user-candidate-count weighted BCE to align training influence with within-user evaluation.
rationale: The official GAUC is a within-user metric, whereas the current row-mean BCE gives prolific users more total optimization weight. The broad spread in user-activity diagnostics makes user balancing a direct, availability-safe objective test rather than a feature expansion.
exact_ablation: Relative to experiment 3, replace the row-mean BCE reduction with BCE weighted by the inverse number of training rows for each user and normalized by total batch weight; retain features, model, optimizer, training rows, split, and early stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by 0.001 to 0.004 if reducing prolific-user dominance better aligns the pointwise objective with within-user discrimination.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Change between -0.001 and +0.002 because equal user weighting need not directly emphasize the first five ranks.

text: Add a small nDCG@5 swap-weighted pairwise ranking term to BCE, using only training-user candidate groups.
rationale: Experiment 3 has adequate aggregate GAUC but notable nDCG@5 failures in sizable tab and hour slices, including tab 0, tab 6, and hour 16. A top-five-focused ranking term directly tests whether optimization rather than missing features limits head ranking.
exact_ablation: Relative to experiment 3, add one detached nDCG@5 swap-weighted within-user positive-negative logistic pair-loss term to the existing BCE objective with a fixed coefficient of 0.1; retain the model, features, optimizer, split, and checkpoint rule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Change between -0.001 and +0.002 because the added loss only supervises mixed-label within-user groups and concentrates on head errors.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.001 to 0.005 if training-user groups represent meaningful candidate competition and top-five misorders are corrected.

text: Replace BCE with a within-user RankNet pairwise loss to optimize positive-negative order directly.
rationale: The failed normalized-dot-product branch demonstrates that changing architecture is risky, while current error diagnosis is principally ranking-oriented. A pure loss replacement isolates direct GAUC alignment without adding features or architecture capacity.
exact_ablation: Relative to experiment 3, replace BCE with a uniformly sampled within-user positive-negative RankNet logistic pair loss using training rows only, with four negatives per positive and equal user weighting; retain features, additive model, optimizer, split, and early stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by 0.001 to 0.004 if sampled within-user pairs faithfully represent the official ordering objective.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Change between -0.002 and +0.002 because an unweighted pairwise loss does not preferentially correct rank-one through rank-five errors.

text: Add a ListNet top-one listwise term to BCE to test whether whole-user candidate competition improves top-five ranking.
rationale: Weak nDCG@5 in large context slices can coexist with nontrivial GAUC, suggesting that a listwise training signal could be informative. This is high-risk because the available archive does not establish that all temporally grouped rows for a user form coherent contemporaneous slates.
exact_ablation: Relative to experiment 3, add exactly one within-user ListNet top-one loss term with coefficient 0.1 to the existing BCE objective, calculated only on complete mixed-label training user groups; retain all features, model parameters, optimizer, split, and early stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Change between -0.002 and +0.002 because listwise normalization can trade broad discrimination for relative group order.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.001 to 0.004 if training groups are coherent candidate lists; otherwise it may decline.

text: Increase L2 regularization on the additive categorical weights to reduce sparse cross-feature overfit.
rationale: The user-by-tab cross improved primary by only 0.000439 over experiment 1, below its predicted gain, and rare items remain weak. A stronger shrinkage test is a clean way to assess whether the sparse new cross is adding variance rather than stable ranking signal.
exact_ablation: Relative to experiment 3, change only L2 regularization from 0.000001 to 0.00001; retain features, additive architecture, BCE loss, learning rate, batching, split, and early stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Change between -0.001 and +0.002; modest improvement is possible if sparse categorical weights are overfit, but excessive shrinkage can reduce discrimination.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Change between -0.001 and +0.002; any gain should come from more stable ordering rather than additional top-rank supervision.

text: Use official-primary validation checkpoint selection instead of GAUC-only proxy checkpoint selection.
rationale: The selection objective is the mean of GAUC and nDCG@5, but the current training code checkpoints on a GAUC proxy alone. Since nDCG@5 is a recognized weakness in several large slices, matching the checkpoint criterion to the fixed official objective is a direct training-only ablation.
exact_ablation: Relative to experiment 3, select and early-stop checkpoints using validation primary, computed as the fixed mean of validation GAUC and validation nDCG@5, instead of the current validation-GAUC proxy; retain all features, loss, model, optimizer, and training data unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Change between -0.001 and +0.001 because the selected epoch may sacrifice a small amount of broad ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.000 to 0.003 if the selected checkpoint better preserves top-five ordering than the GAUC-proxy optimum.

text: Reduce the Adam learning rate to improve optimization stability of sparse categorical interactions.
rationale: Experiment 3's small gain over experiment 1 and the severe regression of the more complex experiment 2 branch argue for a low-cost stability ablation before further capacity expansion. The current additive model includes a sparse user-by-tab table whose updates may benefit from a smaller step size.
exact_ablation: Relative to experiment 3, change only the Adam learning rate from 0.01 to 0.005; retain features, architecture, BCE loss, L2 regularization, batch size, split, and early stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Change between -0.001 and +0.002; lower steps may improve convergence stability but can underfit within the fixed epoch budget.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Change between -0.001 and +0.002; any improvement would reflect a different convergence path rather than direct head-rank optimization.

text: Remove the user-by-tab cross as a rollback ablation to test whether its tiny observed gain generalizes versus added sparse-feature variance.
rationale: The cross improved primary by only 0.000439 relative to experiment 1, while the feature analyst explicitly judged that this was insufficient evidence to fund broader interaction expansion. A rollback test is materially informative because it verifies whether retaining the cross is justified under the scarce-budget protocol.
exact_ablation: Relative to experiment 3, remove exactly the train-fitted user_id × tab categorical feature and its additive weight; retain user_id, video_id, tab, hour, weekday, BCE loss, optimizer, split, and early stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Change between -0.001 and +0.001 because the prior global gain from the cross was very small.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Change between -0.001 and +0.001; a decline would support retaining the cross, while an improvement would indicate that sparse interaction variance harms head ranking.
